tree.allocation_conclusion: C1 and C2 tree paths retain 24-byte Node allocation, header/child initialization, recursive construction and runtime allocation fallbacks. C1 worker calls tree, and the C2 OSR worker retains inlined allocations and recursive tree/check call sites. C1/C2 check retain recursive traversals.

long_lived_root.normal_path_conclusion: The interpreted Main$ frame keeps the long-lived tree reference in local slot 4 across task submission and waiting for all results, then reloads that same reference for the final recursive check. The verified bytecode reference type and later use keep it a GC root during intervening work. This is interpreter liveness evidence; there is no compiled-main OopMap in this invocation.

pidigits_conclusion: The interpreted Main$ caller performs two distinct general Scala BigInt.$div operations, at BCIs 115 and 138, before each reached comparison at BCI 147. Both installed BigInt division versions preserve real division; the small-long path and large-value BigInteger path are legitimate library implementations. This does not claim two BigInteger.divide invocations per iteration or a measured numeric division count.
qualification_basis: All ten actual source/class pairs passed the retained 27 static work contracts and 149 bounded cases. The two identified runtime gaps are closed by this tree review and the separate pi peer review. Qualification applies to those exact frozen implementations and runtime configuration.
limitations: Diagnostic captures are not timing samples.
